title: How long must the second strip be for a rectangle?
description: Two thin strips are the diagonals of a rectangle, and two triangles that share a side show that the diagonals match in length. The video finds the second strip from the first, then answers Keeko's doubt that the second strip can be any length.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonals of a rectangle are equal, shown by two congruent triangles that share a side. Watch for students who think any second strip will do because the thread always makes four sides.

source: The carpenter has one strip 8 cm long. How long must the oth
video_script.why: The child sees that the strips are the diagonals of the frame, and that congruent triangles force the diagonals of a rectangle to be equal.
video_script.substitution: Name the frame as rectangle ABCD, pick two triangles that share a side, match them by SAS, and read off the diagonals.
video_script.anchor: two thin wooden strips crossed on a workbench with a thread through their ends, drawn as rectangle ABCD
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the second strip can be any length because the thread still makes four sides; a different length tilts the shape, so its corners are not right angles.
video_script.payoff_line: The other strip must be eight centimetres long

final_answer.spoken: the other strip must be eight centimetres long

names.Ruhee: the carpenter who joins two wooden strips so that a thread through their ends makes a rectangle

maths_rules: the frame is rectangle ABCD: all four angles are 90 degrees and AB = CD
the two strips are the diagonals AC and BD, and AC = 8 cm
in triangle ADC and triangle DAB: AB = CD, angle BAD = angle CDA = 90 degrees, and AD = DA (common side)
SAS: triangle ADC is congruent to triangle DAB, with A matching D, D matching A and C matching B
matching sides of congruent triangles are equal, so AC = BD
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonals of a rectangle are equal. Wrong idea: the second strip can be any length. The rectangle stays on the board from the ground beat to the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>Here is a question from your book about Ruhee and two strips.
<bookmark mark='thread'/>A thread through the four ends must make a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>One strip is eight centimetres long. How long must the other strip be?

narration: <bookmark mark='frame'/>We draw the thread shape as rectangle eigh B C D.
<bookmark mark='diag'/>A line joining two opposite corners is called a diagonal. Each strip is a diagonal.
<bookmark mark='known'/>Diagonal eigh C is eight centimetres. We need diagonal B D.

beats.on_screen: Given: ABCD is a rectangle, AC = 8 cm

marks.given: the two given facts are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh B C D is a rectangle, and diagonal eigh C is eight centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of the other diagonal, B D.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: in triangles ADC and DAB, AB = CD (opposite sides of a rectangle), angle BAD = angle CDA = 90 degrees (right angles), AD is common

beats.colours: the two triangles in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step one, take triangles eigh D C and D eigh B.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>Side eigh B equals side C D, as opposite sides are equal.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>Angle B eigh D equals angle C D eigh, both being right angles.
<bookmark mark='common'/>Side eigh D is common to both triangles.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: two sides and the angle between them are equal, so by SAS triangle ADC is congruent to triangle DAB

marks.sas: the two equal sides and the angle between them are ticked in both triangles

beats.colours: the two triangles in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='sas'/>Step two, two sides and the angle between them match.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the side angle side rule, the two triangles are congruent.
<bookmark mark='means'/>Congruent means the two triangles match exactly in size and shape.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: matching sides of congruent triangles are equal, so AC = BD

marks.match: AC in the first triangle and DB in the second glow in the same colour

beats.colours: AC and BD in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>Step three, matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>Side eigh C matches side D B, so eigh C equals B D.

beats.on_screen: Answer: BD = 8 cm, because the diagonals of a rectangle are equal

marks.ans: the answer BD = 8 cm is boxed
marks.why: both diagonals glow with the same length

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The other strip must be eight centimetres long.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so B D is eight centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a shorter second strip is swapped in; the thread shape tilts and its corners are no longer right angles

marks.doubt: a second strip of any length is swapped in
marks.fix: the thread shape tilts and the corner marks turn from right angles
marks.rule: the two equal diagonals of the rectangle glow again

beats.colours: the doubt in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the other strip can be any length. The thread still makes four sides.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a shorter strip tilts the shape, so the corners are not right angles.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>A rectangle needs equal diagonals, so both strips must match.
